scope: Paired current-main performance experiment; not a v0.3 regression reproduction or time-to-convergence benchmark.

method.restrictions: Compare within each machine/environment only. GPU first-derivative compilation overlapped other work, so no cold-start speed ratio is claimed. RSS includes host compiler memory; it is not device peak memory.

changes: Reuse jax.linearize of the preconditioned residual across parameter columns and Krylov matvecs. Preserve the derivative of the preconditioner, including dP times finite residual.

Separate m*alpha from (m*iota-n)*phi in Boozer field-line synthesis. Share the exact sine/cosine identity across surrogate QI, constructed QI, bounce tracing and maximum-J pitch selection. Highest dot precision for float32.
No change to grids, modes, Boozer transform, residual normalization, solve tolerances, certificate policy, or SOLVAX algorithms.

component_48_dof.harness: External profile_vmex.py: capture the residual/Jacobian passed by opt.least_squares without invoking the optimizer. The in-tree public optimizer benchmark below is separate.
component_48_dof.input_recipe: The supplied deck has the same physics and Fourier coefficients as examples/data/input.nfp1_QI. Set MPOL=5, NTOR=5, NS_ARRAY=16, NITER_ARRAY=4000, FTOL_ARRAY=1e-12; remove the disabled BOOZ_XFORM_JAX namelist. Its formatting differs, so this recipe does not reproduce the byte hash.
component_48_dof.samples: x_i=x0+i*1e-6*linspace(-0.5,0.5,48); residual followed by Jacobian. CPU i=1..6; GPU i=1,3,4, excluding traced i=2.

gpu_trace.tool: JAX profiler / XProf Chrome trace, GPU kernel events inspected with their HLO metadata
gpu_trace.finding: Short cuSPARSE tridiagonal kernels recur inside GMRES JVPs of the preconditioned residual. Hoisting its exact linearization reduces repeated primal work. Summed kernel durations are not total optimizer wall time.

public_cpu_constructed_qi.command: JAX_ENABLE_X64=1 JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu VMEX_COMPILATION_CACHE=disabled OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=. python benchmarks/optimization.py --case constructed_qi --input examples/data/input.nfp1_QI --keep-input-resolution --max-mode 1 --refine-tol inf --batch-size auto --warm-evaluations 3 --optimizer least_squares --nfev 5 --skip-jax-contract --device cpu --output /tmp/report.json
public_cpu_constructed_qi.baseline_setup: Copy the candidate benchmarks/optimization.py into a detached baseline worktree; keep baseline vmex/ unchanged. Use a separate fresh process and output path for each arm.

public_cpu_constructed_qi.conclusion: Warm Jacobian improves, but capped optimizer wall time does not: 22.816 versus 22.986 s. Both hit the five-evaluation cap; neither is a converged design. No end-to-end speedup claim.

validation: GPU float32/float64 dense-reference values, JVP, VJP; float64 central FD; symmetric/asymmetric and nfp=1,3: 8 passed (11.24 s).
CPU bounce, QI reference, maximum-J, omnigenity, QI residual/composition regressions: 50 passed, 7 skipped (236.37 s; prior helper precision setting, float64).
Combined implicit multi-RHS plus optimizer block/chunk parity: 10 passed, 4 full tests skipped (547.76 s).
RUN_FULL=1 pytest tests/test_omnigenity.py tests/test_qi_residuals.py tests/test_maxj.py -m full: 6 passed (249.09 s), including re-solved finite differences and LASYM.
ruff check vmex tests examples benchmarks tools; mypy vmex: passed (75 source files).
rejected_experiments: Linearize the objective G before directional chunks: CPU 1.14-1.25 s, no useful gain; reverted.
Batch raw-block radial rows in groups of four: about 4% GPU improvement with higher compilation/RSS, less useful than the retained changes; reverted.
limitations: No full collaborator Simsopt run to convergence and no uniform optimization-runtime or precision guarantee from a small benchmark sample.
Field-line derivative temporary allocations fall from approximately 159 MB to 16-18 MB, but forward-only temporary allocation grows from approximately 1 MB to 9 MB.
Refinement is disabled to match the supplied wrapper; this experiment does not justify weakening default refinement or certification tolerances.
The historical v0.3 and current Boozer objectives differ numerically; their raw wall times do not isolate a same-accuracy regression.

gpu_optimizer_blocker.environment: Standalone Python 3.11.15, JAX/JAXlib/cuda12 plugin 0.9.2, NumPy 2.4.6, SciPy 1.17.1, SOLVAX 0.20.0, booz_xform_jax 0.2.0; pip check passed.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.command: Same public constructed-QI command with JAX_PLATFORMS=cuda,cpu, device gpu and one CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES index per process.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.observation: Both arms completed initial compilation and reached scipy TRF trial evaluation. At 660 seconds both were still inside a coarse-grid NS=3 retry, compiling jnp.sum in setup.flux_profiles from the GPU pure_callback. Terminated after approximately 11 minutes. No valid optimizer timing.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.independent_reproduction: On the same GPU environment, jit(pure_callback(callback, scalar_float64, x)) stalls for at least 45 s when callback enters jax.default_device(gpu), creates arange(3) from NumPy and returns np.asarray(jnp.sum(a*a)). Calling callback once before the jitted invocation makes the latter finish in 0.01096 s. Reproduction contains no VMEX code.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.inference: First-use GPU compilation inside a running GPU host callback is a separate runtime/placement hazard. The component speedups do not fix it.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.next_action: Keep nonlinear solve/retry setup outside the compiled host-optimizer residual callback, preserving identical status, penalties, warm seeds and parameter-key memoization. Test direct Jacobian calls and the separate staged JAX API before promoting a fix. Do not change tolerances or add unconditional coarse-grid warmup as a numerical workaround.
gpu_optimizer_blocker.exclusions: Earlier runs with asynchronous faulthandler dumps crashed while dumping; excluded. Safe Python-thread stack sampling was used for this localization.
